Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Libyan Tax Authority announced launch of a “Unified Tax System” and planned digital platforms in 2026, but evidence captured did not confirm active online tax payment at scale; implies partial movement toward digital revenue collection but not yet fully proven.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with stronger, fresher evidence: PM Decree No. 60/2026 (March 2026) legally mandates all government treasuries to accept e-payment for taxes, customs and fees, and CBL (May 2026) is rolling out POS terminals to the Tax, Customs and Ports authorities in phases (130 terminals in phase one), building on Decision No. 247/2024 permitting electronic income-tax collection. Rollout is real but still partial/early-stage, so 'Partial' (code 2) is upheld.

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Tax Authority announced the Unified Tax System and that several digital platforms are scheduled to become operational in 2026, implying an under-development digital tax portal ecosystem (not yet confirmed live).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: The Libyan Tax Authority's official portal ly.tax is live, offering digital registration for individuals/companies and direct electronic payment ('integration with electronic payment systems... completing payment electronically and instantly'). Combined with Decision No. 247/2024 authorising electronic income-tax collection, this is evidence of an operating portal rather than one merely 'under development', so raised from 3 to 4 ('Yes'). Note the portal's confirmed scope centres on business registration and commercial-paper certification rather than full income-tax return filing.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Evidence suggests Libya joined the Pan-African Payment & Settlement System (PAPSS) network (central bank participation), indicating cross-border capability is at least being enabled; however, no evidence found of full, end-user cross-border instant payments already widely functional.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with a materially better source: PAPSS's own June 2026 network-coverage document lists Libya as 'LIVE SOON' rather than among the countries with live send/receive participants (Djibouti, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). This corroborates the Central Bank of Libya's PAPSS membership (~January 2026) while showing onboarding is not yet live, supporting 'Under development' (code 3).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: CBL launched “Ratebk Lahzi” real-time salary transfer platform (public-sector payroll) via the national instant payment network, indicating active G2P use (government salary deposits).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed via the Central Bank of Libya's own site: the 'Instant Salary' (Ratabk Lahzi) system was officially launched 1 September 2025 for around 900,000 public-sector employees and has continued monthly disbursements through at least April 2026. This primary-source evidence base is materially stronger than the single news article originally cited and fully supports 'Yes - Active Use' (code 3).

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: CBL statistics report merchant subscribers/active merchants and POS terminals for OnePay plus purchases via LYPay, indicating person-to-business merchant payments through POS/instant payment services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. CBL's own statistics show tens of thousands of active OnePay merchants and POS terminals with growing purchase volumes, and Libya Herald (February 2026) reports continued unprecedented growth in e-payment app transactions (LYD 313bn by 15 February 2026). Supports 'Yes' (code 2) for P2B merchant payments.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Libya has general personal-data provisions in Law No. 6/2022 on Electronic Transactions (e.g., consent/collection rules for personal data in electronic transactions), but sources do not indicate a dedicated payments-data law.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Libya has no dedicated data-protection act; general personal-data provisions sit within Chapter 7 of Law No. 6 of 2022 on Electronic Transactions (consent, confidentiality and data-subject access rights), corroborated by UNECA's DTRI country profile and Eltumi Partners' legal analysis alongside the original DLA Piper guide. This is general, not payment-specific, legislation, supporting 'General Data Protection Legislation' (code 2).

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: CBL publishes “Instant Payment Services Statistics” for LYPay/OnePay (ad hoc web updates rather than clearly periodic monthly/quarterly series in the evidence captured).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a fuller evidence trail: CBL published at least six standalone 'Instant Payment Services Statistics' releases between August 2024 and January 2025, plus occasional governor briefings citing updated figures (July 2025, March 2026). These are recurring but irregular press-style releases rather than a fixed published monthly/quarterly series, so 'Ad Hoc' (code 2) is upheld rather than upgraded.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: Independent review/audit exists for Central Bank of Libya (not necessarily the payment system operator specifically): UNSMIL reports Deloitte selected as independent auditor for an International Financial Audit Review of CBL branches (final reports transmitted in 2021).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Not supported: the originally cited UNSMIL source concerns a 2021 institutional/unification audit of the Central Bank of Libya as a whole, predating LYPay/OnePay's 2024 launch, and is not evidence of independent audits of the digital payment system itself. A 2025 CBL item shows the Libyan Audit Bureau reviewing CBL's own accounts for 2017-2024 — again not payment-system specific — and CBL's public regulatory documentation only states banks must submit compliance/security reports, without confirming any completed, publicly disclosed independent audit of the payment system. Recalculated to 0 (Unknown/n.a.) for lack of on-point evidence; flagged for human review in case Arabic-language regulatory filings hold further detail.
